fact_checks.rationale: Correct active moiety; FDA SEZABY documents identify phenobarbital sodium and NCBI sources identify phenobarbital/phenobarbitone as the same ASM.
Phenobarbitone is a standard alternate generic spelling used in PubMed/NCBI literature for the same drug.

FDA review supports historical Luminal and FDA approval/orphan records support current SEZABY. Phenobarb/Solfoton were not confirmed from FDA sources in this audit, but no direct contradiction was found, so do not delete them without user approval.

fact_checks.current_value: 1912 legacy; predates modern FDA approval system
fact_checks.proposed_value: 1912 legacy marketing under Luminal before modern FDA approval; SEZABY NDA approved 11/17/2022 for neonatal seizures
fact_checks.rationale: FDA clinical review states phenobarbital was synthesized in 1911 and marketed in 1912 as Luminal, before modern FDA approval requirements, and FDA approval documents give SEZABY approval date 2022-11-17.
NCBI StatPearls lists oral elixir, oral tablets, and IM/IV solution; FDA SEZABY label supports IV injection formulation.

fact_checks.proposed_value: Adults about 75-120 h; children about 21-75 h; neonates approximately 1 week
fact_checks.rationale: The selected FDA label does not support 53-118 h; FDA labeling states neonatal t1/2 is about 1 week, and eMC SmPC reports adult half-life about 75-120 h and pediatric about 21-75 h. Current value should be replaced or separately sourced if retained.
FDA label states phenobarbital is metabolized by CYP2C9 and lesser CYP2C19/CYP2E1/UGTs; NCBI states hepatic microsomal metabolism.

fact_checks.rationale: FDA label identifies induction of CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP2Cs and UGTs; eMC notes induction of hepatic drug-metabolizing enzymes.

fact_checks.rationale: FDA label states the precise mechanism is not fully understood and is thought to involve potentiation of synaptic inhibition through GABAA receptors; NCBI describes increased duration of GABA-A chloride-channel opening.
